title: Rav Chanan bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of Shmuel, citing “Rav Chanan bar Ami said in Shmuel’s name” in [Shabbat 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.111b.2), [Ketubot 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.6a.5), [Gittin 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.52b.10), [Bava Metzia 82b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.82b.2), and [Bekhorot 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.25a.4). Hyman cites Shabbat 13b for this form. In [Shabbat 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.13a.5-6), we find “Rav Chanin bar Ami said in Shmuel’s name,” and in [Chullin 107b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.107b.17) “Rav Chanan.” In [Bekhorot 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.34a.8), “Rav Chanin bar Ashi said in Shmuel’s name” SHOULD READ “Rav Chanan bar Ami,” according to Hyman.

In [Chullin 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.15a.12), Rav Chanan bar Ami said, ‘When Rav would instruct his students, etc.’ Hyman infers from this that he lived in their time and himself heard what Rav said.

[Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:5 (printed 6:8)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.5.2) has ‘Anan k-Rabbi Immi [כרבי אימי].’ Hyman cites [Or Zarua II 84:1 (printed end of chapter 4)](https://www.sefaria.org/Ohr_Zarua%2C_Volume_II.84.1), reading ‘Chanan bar Immi said before Rav Yehudah in the name of Menashe bar Yirmeyah’ (whom Hyman calls Rav’s student).[^4][^5]

notes.text: Anan is a personal name, not “we.” The supplied כרבי and cached Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5 כר׳ have an irregular prefix; Hyman cites 6:8 and offers the son-of reading from Or Zarua. His reconstruction remains attributed.

Both selected digital scalars were freshly read whole: Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat chapter 6, selected halakhah 6:5 scalar, and Zhytomyr 1862 Ohr Zarua II 84:1. Guggenheimer has Anan כר׳ Immi before full Rabbi Yehudah and the distinct irregular Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah sequence; Or Zarua has Chanan bar Immi before full Rav Yehudah in Menashe bar Yirmeyah’s name. These are distinct named digital witnesses, not printed verification or a demonstrated letter-repair history. Hyman supplies 6:8 and end of chapter 4 beside the actual matching 6:5 and II 84:1; neither old locator is silently corrected. The source’s כרבי has an irregular prefix with full Rabbi, beside abbreviated כר׳ in Guggenheimer; the source form is retained. Hyman’s Chanan/Chanin and Ami/Ashi changes and SHOULD READ force remain attributed. Hyman infers personal hearing and chronology; no student or family identity is admitted. All source holds remain.

The consulted Shabbat 111b, Ketubot 6a, Gittin 52b, Bava Metzia 82b and Bekhorot 25a use Chanan bar Ami in Shmuel’s name. Chullin 107b in the consulted edition also has the full Chanan bar Ami. Bekhorot 34a has Chanin bar Ashi in Shmuel’s name, the form Hyman proposes emending. The exact Shabbat 13b reading he reports remains unverified. Chullin 15a transmits Chanan’s statement about Rav’s teaching to his students; whether Chanan heard Rav personally is Hyman’s inference. The consulted Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5 begins with Anan כר׳ Immi addressing Rabbi Yehudah and gives the irregular Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah sequence. The consulted Zhytomyr Or Zarua II 84:1 instead gives Chanan bar Immi addressing Rav Yehudah in Menashe bar Yirmeyah’s name. Hyman’s print cites 6:8 and the end of Or Zarua II, chapter 4.
Heilprin collects further Chanan and Chanin variants, including this transmission from Shmuel. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1416&lang=en).
The two versions on Shabbat 13a both give Chanin bar Ami in Shmuel’s name. The linked Chullin passage gives Chanan bar Ami.
